notes: These vectors pin CBS dual-plane semantics. DataEvent vectors use signed kind + payload + scope_ref + seal_ref and never use preconditions. Control Move vectors use signed kind + payload + scope_ref + seal_basis and may use preconditions. Every cell write is receiver-projected from the registered reducer contract.

Seal delta entries reference only newly sealed control-plane event digests. Cumulative coverage is derived from predecessor_refs[] plus delta[]. DataEvent digests may appear in data_event_set_root / data_view_root observations, but those roots do not confer control-plane finality.
Cell ids follow ak:cell:ak.component.<facet-path>.v<n>:<subject>; subject placeholders use dot-safe strings to keep examples unambiguous.

lattice_round_trip.description: SDK lattice round-trip runner coverage for CBS lattice family vectors exercised through any conforming local lattice implementation.

assertions: an unwritten cell has no head and reads null
each write is identified by its EventId and supersedes exactly the heads observed in its own signed seal_basis
a release write is set null, keeps its own head, and stays distinguishable from an unwritten cell
A -> null -> A reads A, and A -> B -> A -> B reads B
concurrent writes with different values leave two heads and a bottom=reject cell materializes failed_bottom
concurrent writes with the same value keep both head identities and a successor that saw only one of them removes only that one
exact replay of the same identity and canonical effect is idempotent
merging two verified (covered set, heads) states is associative, commutative, idempotent and agrees with a full causal-history oracle
Bottom is recomputed per view, so a receiver that later observes the missing leaf converges with one that saw the full history

vectors.name: cas_mixed_basis
vectors.description: cas_register admission derives the full active-head identity guard from each write's own signed seal_basis and compares it to the frozen predecessor heads at Seal acceptance; equal business values are not enough.

expected.note: With no reconstructable signed basis the reducer cannot derive H_c(B); it MUST fail closed rather than degrade to an unconditional overwrite.
H_c(B) equals the frozen predecessor H_c(P), so the automatically derived identity guard passes. No wire head_eq is required for this cell.

Both the stale basis and the frozen predecessor settle to null, so a whole-value comparison would pass. The head identities differ, so the identity guard rejects the write. This is the ABA case the deleted value-edge join could not express.

control_move.note: The binding cell subject is derived from this Event's own event_id, so writing that cell_id into the digest-covered preconditions would be hash-self-referential.

expected.note: The reducer derives the identity guard after the EventId is computed. Rejecting because preconditions[] carries no head_eq for this cell is non-conforming.

vectors.name: conflict_recovery_move
vectors.description: A bottom=reject control cell recovers only through a sealed ak.conflict.recovery Control Move projected by the registered cell_ref + reset form; no other kind may declare that form. The registered contract names no lattice, so the target cell decides both which conditions apply and what op the reset becomes. For the causal registers (cas_register and fsm, event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.5.1) the reset is a new identity write: the signed basis must show divergent heads, the state_witness inclusion requirement and its freshness window do not apply, recovery supersedes only the heads it observed, and arrival-order truncation is forbidden. The remaining bottom=reject lattices keep the pre-conflict state_witness family of requirements below, so the top-level cases here run on an ordered_log bottom=reject cell rather than on a causal register. Section 9.3.1.4 layers the exit from Bottom: the registered sole_recovery_families have no ordinary-write exit and recovery is their only one, while every other causal-register family also heals through an ordinary write that already holds authority for its action. The list never restricts which cells a recovery may target.

expected.note: reset is legal only on a cell already in bottom; on any other state the write is rejected, so recovery cannot be used as a general overwrite channel.
the state_witness must witness the cell named by payload.target_cell_id; witnessing a different cell proves nothing about the one being reset.

ak.component.mls.epoch.v1 is a registered sole_recovery_families member precisely because this ordinary write reads the cell it would have to heal: the base-epoch precondition fails closed under Bottom, so no Commit can ever advance the epoch again.

section 9.3.1.4: outside sole_recovery_families an authorized ordinary write supersedes every head and converges the cell; it needs no recovery capability and MUST NOT be given a separate reset channel.
self-healing lifts only the extra block that the target sits in Bottom; every other authorization, lifecycle and business precondition still applies.

the authority root is the sole genesis base case of the authorization graph, so its own authorization read fails closed under Bottom and nobody is left to author an ordinary write; only ak.conflict.recovery applies.
sole_recovery_families names where recovery is the ONLY exit; it MUST NOT be implemented as a restriction on which cells a recovery may target, which would strand families that have not been audited.

verifying any Seal first reads the accepted notary configuration, so a recovery Seal for that cell can never be accepted. It is deliberately absent from sole_recovery_families because listing it would imply an exit that does not exist.

assertions: the signed seal_basis MUST show divergent heads on the target cell; a recovery against a non-divergent cell is failed_precondition
no state_witness ref is required and recovery_witness_freshness_window_ms does not apply on this path
the recovery capability is still verified against its registered authority path, including revocation, scope and authority generation
the covering Seal still compares full heads H_c(B) = H_c(P); a branch that entered P forces a new recovery
a late branch the recovery basis never covered still merges, and two concurrent divergent recoveries still conflict
implementations MUST NOT truncate the op history at the last reset by arrival order
the reset projects as a transition carrying only to = payload.resolved_value; a set MUST be rejected because fsm accepts no set
the recovery transition MUST NOT carry a from; under bottom it supersedes two or more divergent heads at once and no single state names them
admission runs the registered allowed_transitions from every superseded head's to into resolved_value; any head with no such edge rejects the Event
an empty head set rejects: empty heads are not the divergent-heads proof section 9.5.1 item 1 requires
a terminal state stays terminal because it carries no outgoing edge but its registered self-loop, so no separate terminal_states lookup is needed
resolved_value in states follows from the same table membership and needs no separate check
the recovery head is superseded like any other write: a later registered transition authored against the recovered state moves the cell on
shared_with_cas_register: no state_witness ref is required and recovery_witness_freshness_window_ms does not apply on this path
the recovery capability is still verified against its registered authority path, including revocation, scope and authority generation
the covering Seal still compares full heads H_c(B) = H_c(P)

vectors.description: Second-phase per-peer alignment of sync/federation.md 4.5.3. Local normalization alone never clears peer_stale; the challenged peer has to disclose, at the exact adjudicated position, a canonical sibling set equal to the verdict. The disclosure face is bounded by the request, so alignment is decidable independently of how long the actor history is.

cases.name: void_all_empty_set_aligns
cases.note: An empty disclosed set is the positive statement that the peer holds nothing at this position; it is not a missing answer.

cases.name: extra_sibling_does_not_align
cases.note: Holding the winner is not alignment; the negative half of the verdict has to hold too. A contradicting disclosure keeps the peer stale and never becomes new fork evidence.

cases.name: undisclosed_position_does_not_align

The automatic complete-heads guard does not catch this, because a successor whose basis already contains the first resolution satisfies H_c(B) = H_c(P).

cases.name: another_peer_alignment_does_not_clear_this_peer

vectors.name: fsm_causal_heads
vectors.description: `fsm` is a causal register whose active heads carry the transition's `to`. `from`, `states` and `allowed_transitions` are admission checks against the write's own signed basis; they are never join-time edges, and the op list is never read as a path. A §9.5.1 recovery write is one of these heads: it carries only `to`, supersedes exactly the divergent heads its basis observed, and is itself superseded by a later transition.

expected.note: The one state difference from `cas_register`: an unwritten `fsm` cell reads the registered initial state, not `null`. It still occupies no leaf.
A sequential fold reading the op list as a path answers differently here; the causal state does not, because supersession comes from each write's own basis rather than from its neighbour in the list.
Deduplicating on `(from,to)` collapses this to the same pair as the ABA case and reads `active`. The identities are what tell them apart.

`c2` is a registered edge out of `active` and its basis observed only `c1`. Reading the self-loop as `active`'s single out-edge rejects it as a `same_from_different_to` conflict, which is the defect this pins.
Two identities, one settled state. Collapsing them loses the head a peer that only saw `d1` must still be told about.

A written cell in `⊥` keeps its leaf, for the same reason a `cas_register` one does: absent from the root, `⊥` and never-written are indistinguishable under a non-membership proof, and they read differently.
Same identity, same canonical effect: one head. Two different identities with the same `(from,to)` are two heads. The two cases must not be conflated.

`g1` is superseded on the left and covered on the right, so it drops. `g3` is unknown to the left, so it survives. Union-of-heads would keep `g1` and intersection would drop `g3`; only the section 9.3.1.8 formula is right.
The write claims `from=archived` but its basis cannot be rebuilt, so the reducer cannot check the admission. It holds; it MUST NOT adopt `to` on the strength of an unverified `from`.

The `fsm` escape from `⊥`. The recovery carries only `to`; it supersedes both divergent heads and becomes the cell's single head. It is not a truncation: the two superseded writes stay in the log and stay superseded.

Recovery does not freeze the cell. An ordinary transition authored against the recovered state supersedes the recovery head and moves on, which is only expressible because the recovery is a head rather than a boundary.

Two authorised recoveries, each superseding the same conflicting pair, disagree on `to`. Recovery is an ordinary identity write carrying only its `to`, so it conflicts like any other; arrival order MUST NOT settle it.

vectors.name: apply_patch_base
vectors.description: An apply_patch resolves against a real object base written by a registered set, or it is refused. event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.3.1.2 leaves no other way to obtain one: a family may not declare an initial_value, so null is not an implicit initialization and the first patch never becomes the object definition. The base must also be usable -- written by a set on the same family and addressing the same subject, since an append or a transition writes no whole value and another subject shape names another object.

expected.note: the patch composes onto the created object, so fields the patch does not mention keep the values create wrote.
no real object base is reachable in the signed basis. The reducer must not treat null or an empty object as an implicit initialization, and must not store a partial effect.
the base belongs to the object the create addressed; a patch aimed elsewhere has no base of its own.
cells are Realm-scoped, so a same-named cell in another Realm is not this object base.

cases.name: circle_create_writes_metadata_atomically_with_its_governance_effects
sequence: ak.circle.create appends the create log, sets metadata and transitions history_access

expected.note: the metadata base is one of the create unit effects. If any required write fails the whole unit rolls back; the governance effects are not dropped to make one object hold one cell.
this family is cas_register with bottom=reject; an unwritten cell reads null and a patch has no base.

expected.authorization: content paths stay bound by allowed_write_fields; track management stays with ak.strand.tracks.update
expected.note: both patches compose on the object create wrote, so neither initializes a second authority for the same Strand.
mv_register exposes both heads over one explicit base; the contract promises causal supersession, not automatic field merging.
J(L) is a pure function of the dependency set, so delivery order must not change the joined value.
create is the only writer that may mint a View; update and reconcile address an existing one.
reconcile is a whole-value set, but it is still not a genesis: it republishes a definition for a View that already exists.
the id is derived from the subject on read. create and reconcile would otherwise leave two value shapes in one cell.
reconcile republishes the definition; it is not a channel for rewriting identity, ownership or reducer-derived fields.
tombstone travels only through update. A late or concurrent active definition must not revive a terminal View.
a whole-value set on mv_register replaces the heads its basis observed; an unobserved concurrent branch stays exposed. A known-good definition is not a privilege to overwrite state it never saw.

vectors.name: accountability_record_sources
vectors.description: ak.component.identity.accountability.v1 carries one accountability record with two registered writers: the standalone ak.identity.accountability_grant and the atomic projection ak.agent.provision writes in its controller PCR. Both key the cell by issuer principal, subject principal and the digested scope set, and both project one closed value, so the same endorsement from either source is one cell and one value rather than two.
vectors.cell_subject: composite(issuer principal, subject principal, string_set_digest(accountability_scope, ak.accountability_scope_set.v1))

expected.note: the provision pins accountability_scope to a const and the grant may carry a string or an array; the shared digest context normalizes both, so a bare string is the one-element set.
normalization deduplicates and sorts, so spelling does not fork the record.
neither source puts its event reference or inner proof into the value. Otherwise two endorsements that mean the same thing would differ only by origin and drive a bottom=reject cell into conflict.
expires_at is omitted rather than written as JSON null, and the server receive time is never used.
the projection reads not_before off the envelope, so two signed times that disagree are refused at admission rather than silently resolved.

cases.name: a_later_grant_revokes_the_provisioned_record
sequence: ak.identity.accountability_grant with grant_status revoked on the same cell

expected.note: revocation invalidates the dependent binding; it is not an Agent lifecycle transition.
cells are Realm-scoped. Amending a provisioned accountability means writing the original controller PCR cell; elsewhere is a separate record.
the subject components are principals, but the full AccountId authorization, Station binding and issuer signature checks still run. Principal equality never implies Account equality.
an exact replay is the same write identity, so it does not supersede the revocation that causally followed it.
actor.md 3.3.1 requires accountable_principal_ids to be backed by an active record from either writer; searching only the general kind would reject a legitimately provisioned Agent.

vectors.name: seal_delta_concurrency_class
vectors.description: A Seal's control delta is one of two shapes and never a mixture: exactly one security_barrier transaction, or a set of non-barrier writes on pairwise disjoint cells. The frozen-predecessor rule means a non-barrier write batched beside a barrier is still judged on the state before that barrier took effect, so at-most-one-barrier would leave the dangerous combination open. The class read is the registered one; it is never switched per request.

expected.note: shape 1: exactly one barrier and nothing else.
a registered bootstrap or re-anchor unit is one transaction, not several writes that happen to travel together.
shape 2: every member is exclusive or merge_safe and the target cells are disjoint.

cases.name: barrier_mixed_with_an_ordinary_write_is_refused
delta: ak.strand.update authorized by a moderation-dependent grant

expected.note: the ordinary write would be judged on the pre-decision baseline, so the actor the decision demotes would still act. The whole Seal is refused rather than one member dropped.
shape 1 admits exactly one. Two barriers would each be judged before the other took effect.
same cell, so the second would be judged on a pre-state the first has already superseded.

ak.moderation.decision is security_barrier whether or not this particular request happens to touch a moderation-dependent grant. An implementation must not downgrade it per request to make a batch fit.

cases.name: cyclic_read_write_dependency_between_two_moderators
cases.pre_state: A and B are both unmarked; the moderation write permission requires the author to be unmarked
delta: W1: A marks B, reads moderation(A), writes moderation(B)
W2: B marks A, reads moderation(B), writes moderation(A)

expected.note: the targets are disjoint and both pass at P, but in either serial order the second author is already disabled by the first. This is a genuine cyclic read-write dependency, so no serialization of the pair exists and the batch must not be accepted. Both writes are security_barrier, so shape 1 already refuses the Seal.
ordering is what makes the pair decidable: whichever lands first disables the other's author, and the second is refused on its own authorization rather than by a batching rule.
lift is a barrier too, so it travels in its own Seal; afterwards A's authorization reads clean.

the or_set state returns to a business value it held before, but the write identities differ. A barrier signer keying its double-sign lock on the business value would refuse the third legal write; the key must be the causal state identity.
no member of a refused delta is applied, and no cell is driven to Bottom on the way: the refusal happens at admission, before any join.
